SuppressedCell.description:
A group whose churn is hidden: its size only, never a rate or a churn count.

``too_few``: fewer than 20 customers. ``cross_partition``: a level whose
training count, with what an earlier release report states and the dataset's
public totals, would give a small validation group by subtraction - hidden
whatever its count. ``withheld``: fewer than 20 churners or 20 stayers, or
showing its churn would let a hidden count be worked out from the tables
together; one word for both, so the reason bounds no count. A rule for this
report, not privacy protection: the dataset is a public sample, and
minimum-cohort suppression is not anonymisation.

post.description:
Score a CSV upload for the batch page: every row, with the inputs it was scored on.

The same body limit, the same ``validate_upload`` contract and the same
``Predictor`` as ``POST /predict/batch``; only the response carries more,
so the page can show each row and export it. Nothing is written to disk.
It shares ``state.BATCH_SLOTS`` with that endpoint: past them, 429 at once.

get.description:
One page of the scored book, filtered and sorted, with a summary of every match.

A page past the end is clamped to the last one, so a stale link still
shows rows. ``outcome`` is ``"withheld"`` and ``status`` is ``"unknown"`` for every test customer. With
``ids``, the summary totals exactly those customers (a page's selection).
The README example and one validation customer per case the single-customer page compares.

The filtered book, or exactly the listed customers, as CSV; every cell spreadsheet-safe.

The outcome column reads ``withheld`` for every test customer.
One customer's inputs and served prediction; the outcome only if it may be shown.

post.description:
Every feature's signed contribution to the served probability.

Measured against the same 100 customers, with the same seed and number of
orderings, on every page: training customers, or - where the book is a
public demo's generated one - generated customers, as ``background`` says.
These attribute the model's output; they say nothing about why a customer
stays or leaves.

get.description:
The cached attributions of a sample of the book's customers, as the explainability page draws them.

``partition`` says whose: the dataset's validation sample (``make explain``),
or a public demo's generated customers (``make demo-data``).

Liveness plus whether a model is actually loaded.

Returns 200 either way on purpose: a health endpoint that fails when the
model is missing tells an operator less than one that reports *why*.
What is being served, where it came from, and what it should not be trusted to do.

Everything the executive overview shows, for the whole book.

What the book determines is computed once per served book; what the
tracked reports say is read on each request, so a re-run of ``make
explain`` shows without a restart.

Selection, calibration, the validation sweep and the served model measured
on validation, plus the recorded test evaluation.

No figure here is computed from the test partition: the test block is the
record ``make evaluate CONFIRM=yes`` wrote for this very artifact, or
nothing.

post.description:
Score a CSV upload.

A plain ``def`` rather than ``async def``: parsing and scoring are
CPU-bound, so FastAPI runs them in its threadpool instead of on the event
loop. At most ``state.BATCH_SLOTS`` uploads are scored at once; another
gets 429 at once.

get.description:
Readiness: 200 only when the model, the book and the built front end are all in place.

``/health`` is liveness and stays 200 while the process runs; this is what a
container health check or a proxy should poll. It reads only what is
already in memory - nothing is loaded, read or scored - and names no reason
or path: the log says why.

Observed churn of the training partition, one- or two-way; small groups' hidden.

A group of fewer than 20 customers keeps only its size, and so does every
group that would let one's churn be worked out from the rest.

The validation partition swept across thresholds under the given assumptions.

Unset assumptions take the configured defaults. The recommendation is the
repository's own rule: the highest threshold within one offer's cost of
the best simulated net benefit. Every money figure is SIMULATED.

The accounts the rules point at first: attention, then watch, then no signals.

``priority`` (the default) orders by level, then the nearest renewal, then the
account ID; ``renewal_asc`` by the nearest renewal; ``mrr_desc`` by MRR, and only
within one ``currency``. ``renewal_within_days`` keeps assessed accounts renewing
within that many days. ``q`` searches the account ID and name. A page past the
end is the last page.

One synthetic account: its latest snapshot, rule assessment, evidence and history.

Each historical assessment reads only that snapshot and earlier ones.

post.description:
Map and validate a CSV of account snapshots, and report what it would import.

Stateless: nothing is stored, logged or committed. A file or a mapping that
cannot be read at all is a 422 with every reason; a readable file gets a
preview, its invalid rows rejected with their reasons.

file.description: CSV of account snapshots, UTF-8, one header row.

mapping.description: JSON object {"source column": "canonical field"}. When sent, it is complete and the only mapping used.
